items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: The whole thing is what happens with a lot of musicians when they play... It’s the same thing with the improvisation that we’re talking about with Sam. When we start we have no idea where it’s going to end... He starts off and structures us and guides us through

ctx.x: I want to talk about that. You just used the word “progressive” to describe your own music, and over the years we’ve had the word free, free jazz, and avante garde. Do you object to any of those terms?

Well avante garde means, you know, new, cutting edge. But this is music that has been played since 1971 you know. So I mean it’s not new anymore. So avant garde is a term — just to put it in a box and everything. And free jazz, if you listen to Sam Rivers and other very sophisticated progressive players, they’re not playing free. There’s a lot of structure in what they’re playing. And I don’t play free. There’s a lot of structure in what I play. I play it freely, but it’s not just playing anything at any time I…

The final structure comes after we completed composing the piece, as it would for any composer, whether they’re Beethoven or Bach or Stravinsky. I mean their structure comes after the piece is completed.
